title: 2014 AMC 12A 7
statement: The first three terms of a geometric progression are \(\sqrt{3},\) \(\sqrt[3]{3},\) and \(\sqrt[6]{3}.\) What is the fourth term?

solutions.text:
Writing the terms as powers of \(3,\) they are \(3^{\frac{1}{2}},\) \(3^{\frac{1}{3}},\) \(3^{\frac{1}{6}}.\) The common ratio is \(\dfrac{3^{\frac{1}{3}}}{3^{\frac{1}{2}}}=3^{-\frac{1}{6}}.\)

The fourth term is \(3^{\frac{1}{6}}\cdot3^{-\frac{1}{6}}=3^{0}=1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Rewrite each term as a power of \(3\): \(3^{\frac{1}{2}},\) \(3^{\frac{1}{3}},\) \(3^{\frac{1}{6}}\)
The common ratio is \(3^{\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{2}}=3^{-\frac{1}{6}}\); multiply the third term by it
